page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is an entry-level virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs backed by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware profile includes 16 GB of system RAM, allocating an elevated 8 GB of memory per core, paired with 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete GPU hardware is present on the instance. The processor supports advanced vector and cryptographic extensions, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and SHA-NI.

Performance benchmarks highlight a noticeable divergence between raw single-core execution and overall multi-core throughput. In synthetic processor evaluations, the server achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 3366.29, placing it in the top tier of tested machines. Conversely, the multi-core stress-ng result of 6732.86 aligns with mid-tier averages, while the Geekbench multi-core score of 3114.0 and PassMark CPU score of 6245.05 fall into the lower quartile due to the two-core ceiling and shared resource model. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth registers at 42.17 GB/sec for reads and 29.45 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput reaches 3.42 million SET operations per second, and static web serving achieves 5.17 GB/sec.

The primary architectural advantage of this configuration is its high memory capacity relative to compute allocations, making it cost-efficient for setups requiring large memory footprints without continuous parallel processing demands. The clear tradeoff is limited compute density and shared CPU scheduling, which hinders heavily threaded compile jobs and medium-to-large language model execution. As a result, the server is suitable for small in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, continuous integration staging nodes, and low-traffic web services that require substantial RAM buffers.
description: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-16GB is a KVM virtual server configured with 2 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor at 2.0 GHz, 16 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of local SSD storage. Providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio without discrete GPU acceleration, the hardware emphasizes memory capacity over compute parallelism. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate high single-thread processor performance with a stress-ng single-core score of 3366.29, though aggregate multi-core metrics such as Geekbench (3114.0) and PassMark CPU (6245.05) reflect the shared two-core limitation. Large uncached memory read bandwidth averages 42.17 GB/sec, while Redis operations reach 3.42 million per second. Offering cost efficiency for memory-dense deployments on a budget, this instance fits lightweight database nodes, background queues, staging servers, and memory-buffered web hosting.
